energy_regime.quote: the first beam circulated on 14 July 1989. Collisions came one month later on 13 August
energy_regime.value: Electron-positron collisions at and above the Z resonance (about 91 GeV, rising to 209 GeV by 2000)

intervals.label: proposal
intervals.note: INSPIRE's date_proposed is recorded at year precision '1982' for DELPHI, L3 and OPAL, and as '1982-01-01' for ALEPH; the day-of-January value for ALEPH looks like a default rather than a sourced day, so all four are treated here as year-precision 1982. name: DELPHI
notes: 'DELPHI: Detector With Lepton Photon and Hadron Identification' per the experiment's INSPIRE long_name (src:delphi-inspire-experiment-record).

home.cern's DELPHI page states 'In December 2000, DELPHI stopped taking data', a month later than the LEP-wide shutdown date of 2 November 2000 quoted for L3 and OPAL and than INSPIRE's own DELPHI date_completed ('2000', year precision only). The home.cern quote is used as the most specific DELPHI-labelled figure; the discrepancy is recorded here rather than silently reconciled.

physics_goals.quote: it has the specific ability, using the Ring Imaging Cherenkov technique, to differentiate between all the various secondary charged particles.
physics_goals.value: Identify every type of secondary charged particle produced at the Z resonance using Ring Imaging Cherenkov detectors, and precisely track short-lived particles with silicon detectors

summary.plain: One of four giant detectors on CERN's LEP electron-positron collider from 1989 to 2000, known for its Ring Imaging Cherenkov detectors that could identify the type of each charged particle produced.
summary.technical: General-purpose LEP detector at interaction Point 8, about 10 m in length and diameter, with roughly 20 subdetectors including a Ring Imaging Cherenkov (RICH) system for particle identification and a high-precision silicon vertex detector. Approved by the CERN LEPC on 18 November 1982; ran from August 1989 with the collaboration numbering about 550 physicists from 56 institutes in 22 countries.

unique_capabilities.quote: The DELPHI detector used the ring imaging Cherenkov technique to differentiate between secondary charged particles
unique_capabilities.value: Ring Imaging Cherenkov (RICH) detectors giving full particle identification of charged secondaries, unique among the four LEP detectors
